# Checkbox — M3 guidance

<!-- Generated by apps/site/scripts/one-off/migrate-guidance.mjs. Do not edit by hand.
     The component pages carry the reference; this file carries the guidance. -->

## Web

### Features

Reach for a checkbox when each choice is independent and more than one can be on: permissions, ingredients, the columns you want in a table. A single checkbox is right for something you agree to separately from anything else — terms, a subscription, a flag. If only one option in a set may be chosen, that is a radio group; if the choice is a single thing you turn on and off and it applies immediately, that is a switch. Give the checkbox a label — an unnamed checkbox is a shape that means nothing to a screen reader.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use when each choice is independent and more than one can be on — permissions, ingredients, table columns.
- Use a single checkbox for something agreed to separately — terms, a subscription, a flag.
- Use indeterminate when some (not all) children below are checked.

**Don't**

- Don't use when only one option may be chosen — that is a radio group.
- Don't use for a single on/off that applies immediately — that is a switch.
- Don't render without a label or `aria-label` — an unnamed checkbox means nothing to a screen reader.

### FAQ

**When do I use indeterminate?**

When the box parents a set where some (not all) children are checked — typically a select-all control. It sets the mixed ARIA state, not just a dash.

**Checkbox, radio, or switch?**

Checkbox for independent multi-choices; radio for one-of-many; switch for a single on/off that applies immediately.

## Native

### Features

Reach for a checkbox when one thing can be chosen or not, independently of anything else. It is a controlled or uncontrolled pressable with a `label`, and the third state is the part people forget exists: `indeterminate` is neither on nor off, and it is what a parent shows when only some of its children are checked. Note that `label` is OPTIONAL — omit it and you have a bare control with no accessible name, which is the same trap as an icon-only button. Set it, or name the control some other way.

### Usage

**Do**

- Use `checked`/`defaultChecked`/`onCheckedChange` — Base UI names, same as web — so the state vocabulary never forks by renderer.
- Reach for `indeterminate` for the neither-on-nor-off third state (a partially-selected group), not for loading.
- Give a labelless box an `accessibilityLabel` — the label falls back to it when there is no visible text.

**Don't**

- Don't use a checkbox for a binary on/off setting that takes effect immediately — that is a switch.
- Don't restyle the box past the M3 `18px`/`2px` treatment — the mark's meaning is in its shape.

### Tokens

| Element | State | Token | Value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Marked box | checked | theme.color.primary | primary fill, 18px box, 2px corners |
| Mark | checked | theme.color.onPrimary | onPrimary glyph (surface when disabled) |
| Unmarked box | resting | theme.color.onSurfaceVariant | 2px onSurfaceVariant border on surface |
| Disabled box | disabled | withAlpha(onSurface, 0.38) | 38% onSurface fill or border — the dim is the state |

### FAQ

**Checkbox or switch?**

A checkbox selects within a form (takes effect on submit); a switch applies its setting immediately. Immediate effect means switch.

**How does this differ from the web checkbox?**

The state vocabulary is identical (`checked`, `indeterminate`). The box is drawn by kern styles rather than the Base UI primitive, and the state is announced through `accessibilityState` instead of ARIA.
